evidence: psycopg2/extensions.py:52 imports parse_dsn from _psycopg (installed psycopg2 under Python 3.11.17 site-packages), and lines 145-167 use it on DSN strings. It is a thin wrapper over libpq PQconninfoParse, which accepts URI and keyword/value DSNs and returns a dict of the options that are set, so 'connect_timeout' is present when the DSN supplies it. Malformed DSNs raise ProgrammingError. sql_runner.py:72-74 uses it this way. The claim is about the dependency's API, so the rejections do not change it.

sql_runner.py:72 calls psycopg2.extensions.parse_dsn(connection_string) in __init__, so a malformed DSN raises at construction. The only shipped construction site is build_sql_runner (factory.py:212-221), called from build_agent (factory.py:69), which get_agent calls (tools/_agent.py:66). The query path wraps this at query_database.py:228-231: 'except Exception as e: logger.exception("agent construction failed"); raise RuntimeError(_INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE) from e'. So the failure is logged and surfaced as a sanitized RuntimeError, not an unguarded crash. prime_agent (_agent.py:107-123) deliberately propagates failures to its caller, which decides whether to block startup; I did not trace that caller. The rejections lines concern PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT and connect_timeout handling and do not cover this claim.

sql_runner.py:77 and :89 skip default injection only when PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT is non-empty. libpq's PQconninfoOptions table maps the connect_timeout keyword to the env var PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT, used when the keyword is unset (documented in libpq parameter keywords and environment variables). I did not open fe-connect.c in this run and am relying on that knowledge of libpq. So an unset keyword reads the env value, which bounds the timeout when it is a positive integer. The edge cases (whitespace-only or malformed values, and an explicit 0 meaning no timeout) are the operator's own environment choice, and the recorded rejection about whitespace covers the whitespace case.

sql_runner.py:81-90: connection_params is built with **kwargs, then connect_timeout is injected only if kwargs.get('connect_timeout') is None and PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT is falsy. A non-None caller value is therefore never overwritten, and there is no duplicate key. A None kwarg stays in the dict with no injection when the env var is set. psycopg2's make_dsn drops None-valued keywords, so that None does not reach libpq. I did not run psycopg2, so that point rests on my knowledge of its behavior. Neither rejection line covers this claim.
